title: Multiplayer Plumbing Pipe Routing 3D Editor
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements a multiplayer plumbing pipe routing 3D editor on a 20x10x20 unit architectural grid. Requirements:

## Scene Setup
- Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (25, 20, 25) looking at origin.
- Add OrbitControls for camera manipulation.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light at (10, 20, 10) with intensity 0.8 and shadow mapping enabled.
- Render a semi-transparent grid floor at y=0 (20x20 units, grid helper with 20 divisions).
- Display colored axis indicators at the origin (R=X, G=Y, B=Z), each 2 units long.

## Pipe System
- Pipes are routed as sequences of connected nodes on a 1-unit snap grid.
- Each pipe segment is a CylinderGeometry (radius 0.15, length = distance between nodes) oriented along the connection axis.
- Support 3 pipe layers: 'water' (blue, 0x3388ff), 'gas' (yellow, 0xffcc00), 'drain' (gray, 0x888888). Each layer can be toggled visible/hidden.
- Pipe nodes are shown as small SphereGeometry (radius 0.22) at each junction.
- Elbow joints (90-degree bends) get a TorusGeometry segment (tube radius 0.15, arc Math.PI/2) to show the curve.
- Collision detection: pipes from different layers cannot occupy the same grid edge. Same-layer pipes cannot overlap.

## Multiplayer Simulation
- Simulate 2 players: 'PlayerA' (cursor color green 0x00ff88) and 'PlayerB' (cursor color magenta 0xff00ff).
- Each player has a visible 3D cursor (wireframe box, 1x1x1) at their current grid position.
- Press Tab to switch active player. The active player's cursor pulses (scale oscillates 0.9-1.1).
- Each player maintains their own pipe route in progress and completed pipes list.

## Pipe Routing Interaction
- Click on the grid floor (raycasting) to place the active player's cursor at that snapped grid position.
- Press 'S' to start a new pipe route at the cursor position. This sets the route start node.
- Press 'N' to add the current cursor position as the next node in the active route (must be exactly 1 unit away on one axis from the last node — cardinal directions only).
- Press 'E' to end/finalize the current route, converting it into a completed pipe.
- Press 'U' to undo the last placed node in the current in-progress route (not finalized pipes).
- Press 'D' to delete the most recently finalized pipe of the active player entirely.
- Press '1','2','3' to switch active pipe layer to water/gas/drain respectively.

## Flow Simulation
- Press 'F' to run a flow simulation on all finalized pipes. For each pipe, animate a small sphere (radius 0.1, emissive matching pipe color) traveling from the first node to the last node at 2 units/second.
- Track total flow length across all pipes (sum of all segment lengths).
- Flow particles should be visible and moving simultaneously on all visible pipes.

## Validation System
- Press 'V' to validate all pipes. Validation checks:
  - No overlapping segments across different pipes (collision check).
  - All segments are axis-aligned (no diagonal segments).
  - No pipe has zero-length segments.
- Store validation result as { valid: bool, errors: number }.

## HUD / DOM UI
- Top-left panel showing: active player name, active layer name, number of finalized pipes (total), current route node count.
- A row of buttons: [Start Route] [Add Node] [End Route] [Undo Node] [Delete Pipe] [Validate] [Flow Sim] — these mirror the keyboard shortcuts.
- Layer toggle checkboxes for water/gas/drain visibility.
- A status bar at the bottom showing last action performed as text.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- activePlayer: 'PlayerA' | 'PlayerB'
- activeLayer: 'water' | 'gas' | 'drain'
- playerA: { cursorPos: {x,y,z}, currentRoute: [{x,y,z},...], finalizedPipes: [{ layer: string, nodes: [{x,y,z},...], segmentCount: number }] }
- playerB: { same structure as playerA }
- totalFinalizedPipes: number (sum of both players)
- totalSegments: number (sum of all segment counts across all finalized pipes)
- flowSimRunning: boolean
- totalFlowLength: number (sum of all finalized pipe lengths)
- validationResult: { valid: bool, errors: number } | null
- layerVisibility: { water: bool, gas: bool, drain: bool }
- lastAction: string (description of last action performed)
- undoCount: number (total undo operations performed)
- cursorSnapped: bool (whether cursor is on grid)

All positions must be snapped to integer grid coordinates. Update __3D_STATE__ synchronously after every action.
physics_constraints: Pipes must be axis-aligned (segments only along X, Y, or Z). No two pipe segments from different pipes may occupy the same grid edge. All node positions must be integer-snapped. Flow speed is constant at 2 units/second. Total flow length must equal the sum of Euclidean distances of all finalized pipe segments. Undo must restore exact previous state. Collision detection must be symmetric across layers.
